name: Cultural feminism
summary: Cultural feminism holds that women and men differ in fundamental ways and that women's traits, such as nurture, cooperation, intuition, connection to nature and nonviolence, should be revalued and made the basis of a better culture. It locates the root of oppression in patriarchy and male aggression and responds by building women's institutions, businesses and culture, and by campaigning against pornography and sexual violence. Critics call it essentialist and say it shifted feminism from politics to culture.
scope: The late-1970s and 1980s American strand that Echols, Alcoff and others named cultural feminism, drawn from Mary Daly, Adrienne Rich and Susan Griffin, with the anti-pornography wing (Dworkin, Brownmiller) and the care-ethics thread (Gilligan, Ruddick) as relatives; earlier precursors Jane Addams, Charlotte Perkins Gilman and Margaret Fuller supply the primary source on women's civic and peace virtues. The movement's own writers address few economic, constitutional or foreign-policy questions, so many answers are low-confidence inferences from its anti-militarist, anti-patriarchal and care-centred principles. It excludes liberal, socialist and poststructuralist feminism.

keyFigures.name: Mary Daly
keyFigures.role: Philosopher and theologian whose Gyn/Ecology is cited as a central cultural feminist work.

keyFigures.name: Adrienne Rich
keyFigures.role: Poet and essayist who distinguished motherhood as experience from motherhood as institution.

keyFigures.name: Susan Griffin
keyFigures.role: Author of Woman and Nature, described as central to the theory.

sources.title: Cultural feminism
sources.author: Wikipedia
sources.usedFor: Definition, essentialism, women's values, Rich, Daly, Griffin, anti-pornography movement, feminist businesses, critiques.

sources.title: Mary Daly
sources.author: Wikipedia
sources.usedFor: Daly's view of patriarchy as religion, biophilia, vegetarianism, rejection of male God, trans positions, women-only teaching.

sources.title: Newer Ideals of Peace
sources.author: Jane Addams (1906)
sources.usedFor: Precursor primary text: nurture versus conquest, rejection of war virtues, women's civic housekeeping. Only the first part of the long text was read.

sources.title: Feminist Ethics
sources.author: Stanford Encyclopedia of Philosophy
sources.usedFor: Gilligan's care perspective, Ruddick's maternal thinking, essentialism critiques.

universal-healthcare.rationale: Care ethics treats meeting dependent bodies' needs as a public responsibility, so state-guaranteed health care is a likely inference; the sources do not discuss health policy.

raise-minimum-wage.rationale: Inferred from concern with women's undervalued, low-paid labour; the sources do not discuss wage floors.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: Cultural feminists favoured women's cooperative and 'feminist' businesses over profit competition (s1), implying scepticism of market primacy, though they did not reject markets outright.

public-ownership.rationale: Adherents ran women-owned cooperative enterprises rather than campaigning for nationalisation; the sources give no position on utilities.

tax-the-wealthy.rationale: Addams-style concern for the needs of the poor and industrial reform implies support for redistribution; not a defining cultural feminist demand.

unions-good.rationale: Addams's social-reform tradition backs collective protection of working women and children, but cultural feminists rarely made unions a theme.

property-fundamental.rationale: Care-centred, communal ethics rank relationships and need above owners' absolute rights; inferred, not stated in the sources.

regulate-corporations.rationale: Addams's industrial-legislation tradition supports regulating work and production to protect life; later cultural feminists said little on corporations.

cut-welfare.rationale: Care ethics holds that society must attend to vulnerable people who need care (Ruddick via SEP), which is at odds with the dependency critique of welfare.

worker-ownership.rationale: Feminist cooperative businesses exist in the movement, but critics found them hierarchical and the sources give no worker-ownership programme.

surveillance-ok.rationale: Distrust of male-run state power and focus on bodily autonomy suggest opposition to security-justified surveillance; inferred only.

legalize-drugs.rationale: Cultural feminism did not address drug policy; adherents' views are split between harm-reduction and anti-vice moralism.

restrict-hate-speech.rationale: The movement favoured legal curbs on speech seen as degrading women, as in anti-pornography ordinances (s1), which suggests sympathy for restricting hate speech.

strong-leader.rationale: Hierarchical, male-coded rule is what Daly describes as patriarchal; rule by one strong leader is inferred to be rejected.

state-harmful.rationale: Cultural feminists sought to reform and use law (e.g. anti-pornography ordinances) rather than abolish the state, though they saw it as male-dominated.

limit-guns.rationale: Addams's nurture-versus-conquest ethic and the movement's association of male violence with patriarchy make strict gun limits a natural position; not explicit in the sources.

empower-police-military.rationale: Addams contrasts nurture with militarism and rejects war virtues; cultural feminists tie militarism to male aggression, so expanding the military is opposed.

legalize-sex-work.rationale: Cultural feminism is closely associated with the anti-pornography movement and a conservative 'female standard of sexuality' (s1), and viewed commercial sex as exploitation of women.

decide-locally.rationale: Women's separate communities and local culture are valued, but the sources give no stance on devolution.

rehabilitation.rationale: Care-and-responsibility ethics favours repair and relationships over retribution; inferred, as the sources do not discuss prisons.

traditional-family.rationale: Rich treated motherhood as an institution that controls women (s1) and Daly saw patriarchy as the core problem, so the traditional patriarchal family is not endorsed, although authentic mothering is valued.

same-sex-marriage.rationale: Lesbian-feminism was central to the movement, but marriage as an institution was viewed critically, so support is inferred and uncertain.

abortion-legal.rationale: Rich opposed patriarchal control over motherhood and women's bodies (s1); legal abortion follows from women's control of reproduction, though few sources address it directly.

more-religion-public.rationale: Daly rejected Christianity as patriarchal and called herself post-Christian (s2); adherents oppose a larger public role for male-led institutional religion.

correct-racial-injustice.rationale: Cultural feminism was criticised for neglecting women of colour (Lorde), but its egalitarian commitments would generally favour redress; inferred.

gender-social-construct.rationale: Cultural feminists treat gender differences as fundamental and reject the view that they are mainly social (s1).

preserve-national-culture.rationale: Women's culture, not national culture, is the focus; the sisterhood ideal is cross-national, so national tradition is not prized.

gradual-change.rationale: Daly sought radical transformation of the patriarchal 'foreground', not gradual change within established institutions.

reduce-immigration.rationale: Global sisterhood ideal (s1) points away from restriction; the sources do not discuss immigration.

empower-international-orgs.rationale: Addams's newer ideals of peace imagine shared moral consciousness across nations; support for international bodies is inferred.

free-trade.rationale: Concern for nurture and local labour conditions makes trade liberalisation unlikely to be championed; not discussed in sources.

nation-first.rationale: Addams's peace ideals and the global sisterhood idea (s1) reject putting national interest ahead of cooperation.

humanitarian-intervention.rationale: Opposition to militarism makes force abroad doubtful even for rights; adherents are somewhat split, inferred.

open-borders.rationale: Global sisterhood supports solidarity, but open borders were not a cultural feminist demand.

limit-growth.rationale: Daly and Griffin tie domination of nature to patriarchy (s1, s2), suggesting sympathy for limiting growth; not stated outright.

drastic-climate-action.rationale: Daly's biophilic stance sets male-centred hostility to living things against women's connection to nature (s2), implying strong action to protect it.

tech-solves-problems.rationale: Daly saw the male foreground as necrophilic and hostile to life, and Fuller opposed Enlightenment mechanism (s1); technological optimism is rejected.

expand-nuclear.rationale: Associated with male militarism and the necrophilic domination of nature in Daly's account; not explicit in sources.

revolution-justified.rationale: Daly sought radical change but cultural feminists stressed nonviolence and women's culture, so adherents are split on revolution.

experts-over-public.rationale: Distrust of male-dominated expert institutions, such as Daly's critique of gynaecology, is evident; the question itself is not addressed.

central-planning.rationale: No cultural feminist case for central planning; decentralised women's institutions were preferred.

socialized-markets.rationale: The sources do not address market socialism; feminist cooperatives suggest openness but adherents are not united.

land-value-tax.rationale: Not discussed by the sources; no basis for a position.

tax-inheritance.rationale: Not discussed; neither supported nor opposed in cultural feminist writing.

basic-income.rationale: Care ethics might favour income for care but the movement left no position; adherents split.

state-directs-investment.rationale: Cultural feminists favoured women's own enterprises, not state-led industrial strategy; inferred.

widespread-small-property.rationale: Women-owned small feminist businesses were promoted as a way past patriarchal barriers (s1), consistent with wide small ownership.

abolish-money-wages.rationale: Not discussed in the sources; cultural feminists built women-run businesses paying wages rather than abolishing wage labour.

abolish-central-banks.rationale: No cultural feminist support for market-fundamentalist monetary proposals; inferred from general leanings.

corporatist-bargaining.rationale: State-recognised bodies setting wages are not part of cultural feminism; inferred.

one-party-rule.rationale: Hierarchical rule by a single ideological party is the sort of patriarchal power Daly opposed; adherents would reject it.

monarchy-legitimate.rationale: Hereditary male-dominated rule is patriarchal; Daly's critique of male authority implies rejection, though unstated.

democracy-best.rationale: Addams treats the franchise and civic participation as tools, and women's inclusion in politics is central; support for democracy is inferred.

natural-rulers.rationale: Daly rejects male claims to superiority and authority over women; natural rule is a patriarchal myth to adherents.

political-violence-never.rationale: Addams contrasts nurture with conquest and replaces war virtues with good will; cultural feminists link violence to male aggression (s1).

war-builds-character.rationale: Addams argues that defending war as ennobling means borrowing virtues from a former age and proposes nurturing life as the newer heroism.

separate-church-state.rationale: Daly saw male-led religion as sustaining patriarchy; separation limits its public power.

laws-from-scripture.rationale: Daly called patriarchal religion the source of oppression and rejected scripture-based authority.

private-courts-defense.rationale: Not discussed; privatised force runs against the nurture ethic and women's reliance on public protection.

military-superiority.rationale: Addams opposes the militarist spirit and 'war virtues'; cultural feminists associate militarism with male aggression.

ethnic-nation.rationale: The sisterhood ideal is cross-ethnic, and ethnic exclusivity was criticised in the movement; the sources do not state this directly.

class-struggle-history.rationale: Cultural feminists place patriarchy, not class, at the centre, and Daly's analysis centres male domination (s1, s2).

equal-outcomes.rationale: Cultural feminism valued difference over sameness (s1); Daly opposed equality frameworks (s2) as a diversion, so no clear endorsement.

indigenous-land-authority.rationale: Respect for nature and non-European women's heritage is a point of critique of the movement; support is inferred.

civilizational-union.rationale: Global sisterhood, not civilisational blocs, is the cultural feminist solidarity; inferred.

self-interest-moral.rationale: Care ethics emphasises responsibility and relationships over self-interest (Gilligan, SEP).

duties-before-rights.rationale: Gilligan's morality of responsibility is distinct from rights, but she sees them as complementary rather than ranked, so adherents split.

nature-intrinsic-value.rationale: Daly set patriarchal culture against a "Background" of connection among all living things; this is one figure's view rather than a documented position of the strand.

limit-population.rationale: Rich and others contested control over women's reproduction; population targets conflict with that, so adherents split.

industrial-civilization-disaster.rationale: Daly and Griffin trace a male-made war on nature and life (s1, s2), which suggests agreement though not stated in these terms.

accelerate-technology.rationale: Fuller's organic worldview against mechanism and Daly's critique of necrophilic male culture oppose accelerating disruptive technology.

human-enhancement.rationale: Daly's critique of gynaecology and 'male surgical intrusion' (s2) suggests suspicion of technological bodily alteration.

algorithmic-government.rationale: Impersonal rule by algorithm conflicts with care and relational ethics; inferred.

restore-past-order.rationale: Daly sought to overthrow the patriarchal order, not restore one.

results-over-ideology.rationale: Cultural feminism was a committed ideological project; pragmatic ideology-free policy is unlikely to be central.

direct-action.rationale: Cultural feminists did build separate women's institutions and culture, but the sources give no stance on elections vs direct action.

means-match-ends.rationale: Addams's nurture-versus-conquest ethic holds that methods should embody the aims; women's separate institutions prefigure the desired culture.

return-to-foraging.rationale: Daly's Background of living things is valued, but there is no programme of returning to foraging.

abolish-division-of-labor.rationale: Not a cultural feminist theme; valuing women's distinct contributions implies keeping differences in activity.

distribute-by-need.rationale: Care ethics responds to need; the movement did not formulate a distributive principle.

production-for-use.rationale: Addams's nourishing of human life over profit and care ethics suggest production for need; inferred.

profit-exploitation.rationale: Cultural feminism centred patriarchy, not capitalist exploitation, and critics said its businesses exploited employees (s1).

dictatorship-of-proletariat.rationale: Class dictatorship is foreign to cultural feminism and to its nonviolent, care-based ethic.

capitalism-causes-war.rationale: Addams blamed militarism and war virtues rather than capitalism as such; cultural feminists blamed patriarchy.

taxation-theft.rationale: Addams's tradition treats public provision for nurture as a civic duty; libertarian tax scepticism is alien to it.

harm-principle.rationale: Adherents wanted law to restrict pornography for harm to women yet defined harm broadly, which fits poorly with a narrow harm principle; split.

individual-rights-only.rationale: Care ethics gives weight to relationships and group-linked responsibility over a purely individual rights frame (Gilligan, SEP).

conscription.rationale: Rooted in Addams's rejection of war virtues and cultural feminists' association of militarism with male aggression.

exit-over-voice.rationale: Women's inclusion in political voice was central; exit is not prioritised.

state-as-business.rationale: Addams-style civic housekeeping treats government as caring for life, not as a business serving customers.

positive-liberty.rationale: Care ethics and Addams's emphasis on means for nourishing life imply freedom requires material support; inferred from principles.

media-academia-power.rationale: Cultural feminists saw male-dominated institutions as power-holders, but not primarily universities and media above elected officials.

hereditarian-race.rationale: Cultural feminists reject biological hierarchy among people while assigning women's difference to biology; the race claim is not discussed but runs against their egalitarianism.

organic-representation.rationale: Not discussed; women's own organisations were valued but not as a substitute for parties.

total-state.rationale: Daly opposed male-controlled power and total direction of life is incompatible with women's autonomy; inferred.

national-rebirth.rationale: Cultural feminism sought a rebirth of women's culture, not of the nation.

territorial-expansion.rationale: Addams rejects conquest and war virtues; cultural feminists associate expansion with male aggression.

personal-loyalty-rule.rationale: Oath-based lordly authority is a male-hierarchical form Daly critiques.

bound-labor.rationale: Addams's ideal of nourishing human life and cultural feminism's anti-domination stance oppose bound labour.

no-neutral-knowledge.rationale: Fuller and later cultural feminists privileged women's emotional, intuitive knowing against the Enlightenment's claimed neutrality; Daly's Background/foreground divide treats male knowledge as power-laden.

universal-morality.rationale: Gilligan's different-voice thesis holds that moral reasoning differs, and the movement rejected male universals, though some universalism persists.

single-common-good.rationale: Care ethics' emphasis on particular relationships is at odds with a single reason-derived good; inferred.

jewish-state-israel.rationale: The sources do not address Israel; cultural feminists were not united.

revive-national-language.rationale: Daly proposed a new women's language but not national language revival; no position.

workplace-democracy.rationale: Addams-era industrial reform and critique of hierarchical feminist businesses (s1) suggest support for democratic workplaces; inferred.

school-vouchers.rationale: Not discussed; a public-service orientation makes vouchers unlikely to be favoured.

avoid-deficit-stimulus.rationale: Not discussed; care spending priorities suggest tolerance of deficits.

economic-freedom.rationale: Not discussed; the movement did not prioritise economic freedom for liberty.

national-self-determination.rationale: Not discussed; women's autonomy was the focus.

force-without-un.rationale: Addams-style rejection of war virtues and militarism opposes unilateral force.

reason-over-faith.rationale: Fuller and cultural feminists valued emotional and intuitive knowing alongside reason (s1), against reason as the only guide.

welfare-for-citizens.rationale: The global sisterhood ideal opposes dividing support by citizenship; inferred.

work-for-welfare.rationale: Care ethics values unpaid care as labour, which clashes with work conditions that ignore it; inferred.

class-collaboration.rationale: Addams's civic cooperation and nonviolent conflict resolution favour partnership over class struggle.

sacrifice-heritage.rationale: Cultural feminists sought to recover women's heritage and culture, so destroying inherited institutions is unlikely to be endorsed.

workers-nation.rationale: Not discussed; the movement stressed global sisterhood over national lines.

distinct-gender-roles.rationale: Cultural feminists revalue women's traits but fight patriarchy; they do not want law to impose distinct public roles, whatever their essentialism.

racial-segregation-law.rationale: Cultural feminism's sisterhood ideal and egalitarianism reject legal racial segregation; not explicitly addressed.

state-class-instrument.rationale: Cultural feminists see the state as male-dominated rather than a ruling-class tool.

expand-fossil-fuels.rationale: Daly's biophilia and view of male domination of nature oppose expanding fossil fuel extraction.

assimilate-immigrants.rationale: Not discussed; the movement's attention to heritage and culture suggests respect for others' culture.

elite-replacement.rationale: A conspiracy theory not found in the sources and at odds with sisterhood across groups.

proportional-representation.rationale: Support for fuller women's representation suggests openness to PR; not discussed.

national-mission.rationale: Addams opposes national conquest and war virtues; exporting a national system is alien to the movement.

patriarchy-structural.rationale: Daly argued that men throughout history have sought to oppress women and called patriarchy a religion sustained by identifiable practices.

political-elite-corrupt.rationale: The sources do not address political corruption; adherents would see male political power as the problem, not corruption per se.

heritable-defect-limits.rationale: Eugenic coercion violates women's control of reproduction, a central theme for Rich (s1).

security-forces-accountable.rationale: Accountability for violence matches the movement's opposition to violence; not explicit in sources.

night-watchman-state.rationale: Addams treats active public provision for life as a civic task; minimal state is alien to cultural feminism.

discourage-race-mixing.rationale: Racist discrimination contradicts the sisterhood ideal; not directly addressed.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: Gilligan argued that care and justice are both valid; women's equal worth is basic, but cultural feminists emphasise difference.

restrict-conversion.rationale: Daly's rejection of religious authority over individuals suggests opposition to restricting conversion; not stated.

ban-cattle-slaughter.rationale: Daly was an ethical vegetarian but the sources show no stance on legal bans.

no-religion-state-schools.rationale: Daly saw male-centred religion as sustaining patriarchy; adherents prefer secular schooling.

state-strengthens-encirclement.rationale: Strengthening a state is the opposite of the movement's aims; inferred.

consent-of-governed.rationale: Women's franchise and participation are central to Addams; support for consent as the basis is inferred.

population-transfer.rationale: Forced removal of minorities violates the nurture and nonviolence ethic.

initiating-force-wrong.rationale: Nonviolence is central but a categorical rule includes property, which the sources do not discuss.

competition-drives-progress.rationale: Jane Addams and Gilman argued cooperation, caring and nonviolent conflict resolution are the virtues needed (s1); competition and struggle are the male model.

freedom-as-non-domination.rationale: Domination is the central evil in Daly's analysis of patriarchy, so freedom from arbitrary power is welcome though the republican terminology is not used.

vanguard-party.rationale: Hierarchical vanguards conflict with the movement's rejection of male-style hierarchy and with its focus on women's culture.

priority-to-poor.rationale: Care ethics' attention to vulnerable people requiring care (Ruddick via SEP) supports prioritising the needy.

restrict-strikes-picketing.rationale: Addams-style labour reform sided with workers' protection; inferred.

population-causes-poverty.rationale: Cultural feminists blamed patriarchal institutions, not population, for oppression; not discussed for poverty.

diversity-weakens-cohesion.rationale: Sisterhood across differences is the ideal, although critics say it erases differences (s1); inferred.

emergency-suspend-protections.rationale: Suspension of protections serves force and domination, against the movement's nonviolent and anti-authoritarian stance; inferred.

price-controls-essentials.rationale: Addams's concern for nourishing life suggests support for protecting access to essentials; inferred.

party-controls-media.rationale: Control of media by a ruling party is the male power centre they oppose; adherents also favoured women's own presses.

party-commands-army.rationale: Militarised party authority runs against Addams's rejection of militarism.

long-naturalization-wait.rationale: Not discussed; global sisterhood suggests more welcoming rules.

party-discipline-binding.rationale: The movement distrusted male-style hierarchy and discipline; inferred.

pool-sovereignty.rationale: Addams's newer ideals of international moral consciousness lean toward supranational cooperation; inferred.

head-commands-forces.rationale: Concentrating command of forces in one head is militarist; inferred.

church-by-bishops.rationale: Daly rejected male church hierarchy as patriarchal.

clerical-rule.rationale: Daly rejected rule by male religious authority.

defeat-own-government-war.rationale: Opposition to war is clear, but this specific revolutionary-defeatist tactic is not discussed.

censor-art-for-virtue.rationale: The movement sought restrictions on pornography for harm to women but not general censorship of art for virtue; adherents split.

unlimited-reelection.rationale: Not discussed; opposition to concentrated personal power is inferred.

end-foreign-alliances.rationale: Addams's peace ideals favour dismantling military blocs; inferred, not explicit.

abolish-rental-housing.rationale: Not discussed; no cultural feminist programme for forced home ownership.

people-in-arms.rationale: Armed citizenry runs against the nurture-over-force ethic.

rural-life-healthier.rationale: Daly's valuing of nature is not a rural-versus-urban moral claim; split.

educated-out-of-touch.rationale: Cultural feminism arose partly in academic and literary circles (Daly, Rich); inferred opposition to anti-intellectualism.

cultures-equal-different.rationale: Lorde criticised the movement for ignoring non-European heritages, and the movement ranked women's culture above male culture; no clean position.

death-penalty.rationale: Addams-style nurture ethic and nonviolence favour opposing execution; not explicit.

sex-ed-in-schools.rationale: Cultural feminists sought women's knowledge and control of bodies; sex and gender equality education fits that goal.

creationism-in-schools.rationale: Daly rejected patriarchal religion; teaching creationism in public schools is opposed.

restrict-pornography.rationale: Cultural feminism is closely associated with the anti-pornography movement (Echols), and Dworkin and Griffin are listed among its figures.

citizenship-by-descent.rationale: Not discussed; descent-based citizenship conflicts with global sisterhood.

minority-language-support.rationale: Cultural feminists valued recovering suppressed cultures and a women's language (Daly); inferred.

religious-exemptions.rationale: Daly was critical of religion's hold on women, but exemptions for minorities are not discussed; split.

encourage-eccentricity.rationale: Daly urged women to reclaim 'Hag', 'Witch' and 'Lunatic' (s2), but cultural feminists also pressed conformity to a female standard of sexuality (s1).

sovereign-debt-cancellation.rationale: Addams-style moral concern for the poor suggests support; inferred.

restrict-freedoms-for-growth.rationale: Growth at the cost of domination is rejected; inferred from Daly's critique of necrophilic foreground.

rich-countries-aid-poor.rationale: Addams's moral consciousness across nations and care ethics suggest a duty to aid; inferred.

independent-nuclear-deterrent.rationale: Nuclear weapons exemplify militarism rejected by Addams and the movement.

no-land-for-peace.rationale: Addams-style peace ideals suggest preferring settlements over territorial claims; inferred.

property-serves-common-good.rationale: Addams treats activity as serving civic life; care ethics gives primacy to relationships; inferred.

precautionary-principle.rationale: Daly's biophilic critique of male domination of nature supports caution about harm to living things.

collective-defense.rationale: Alliance-based war commitments conflict with Addams's rejection of war virtues; inferred.

subordinate-church-to-state.rationale: Daly opposed church power but did not argue for state control of religion; split.

force-to-prevent-secession.rationale: Using force to hold a region conflicts with the rejection of war virtues.

sacred-ruler.rationale: Divine male rule epitomises patriarchal religion which Daly rejected (s2).

flat-income-tax.rationale: Addams's reform tradition prefers redistribution via progressive burdens; inferred.

character-from-environment.rationale: Cultural feminists attribute enduring differences to female nature and biology (s1), against pure environmentalism, though Rich attributes the harms of motherhood to institution.

sovereign-above-law.rationale: Unchecked male authority is the patriarchal form Daly opposes.

space-expansion.rationale: Technological conquest runs against organic worldview and biophilia; inferred.

leader-cult.rationale: Cult of male leaders epitomises patriarchal power; inferred.

equal-parenting.rationale: Rich saw motherhood as a distinctly female experience that patriarchy damages, and cultural feminists valued the mother-daughter bond (s1); a presumption of equal time is not their emphasis.

co-ethnic-territorial-claim.rationale: Territorial claims on ethnic grounds are conquest-oriented and nationalist, at odds with the sisterhood ideal and Addams's peace views.

apostasy-punishable.rationale: Daly left Christianity and opposed religious coercion.

women-must-cover.rationale: Compulsory covering of women is male control of women's bodies, which cultural feminists oppose.

kin-peoples-union.rationale: Ancestry-based political unity conflicts with global sisterhood; inferred.

material-conditions-drive-history.rationale: Cultural feminists locate change in patriarchal power and women's culture and values, not in modes of production.

ban-cartels.rationale: Addams-era reform tradition opposes concentrated economic power harming ordinary life; inferred.

courts-bound-by-majority.rationale: Movement sought legal protections for women against majority male power; inferred.

gender-parity-bodies.rationale: Cultural feminism valued women's distinct perspective and presence in public life (Addams on women's civic role), so equal representation follows.

economic-self-sufficiency.rationale: Bloc autarky is a militarist-imperial project; inferred.

trade-labor-env-standards.rationale: Addams's industrial-legislation tradition and biophilia support binding standards; inferred.

moral-incentives.rationale: Not discussed; Addams stresses civic duty but sources give no wage-incentive position.

armed-group-creates-revolution.rationale: Armed vanguards are violence-based and male-coded, against the nurture-over-conquest ethic.

abolish-hereditary-privilege.rationale: Hereditary male privilege is part of patriarchy; inferred.

history-own-civilization.rationale: Women's heritage, not national civilization, is the movement's historical focus.

civilizing-tutelage.rationale: Lorde criticised the movement for ignoring non-European women's heritage; rule over 'less advanced' peoples conflicts with the sisterhood ideal.

patriotic-education.rationale: Addams criticised war virtues as a basis for civic loyalty; pride in flag and anthem is militarist-coded.

end-racial-preferences.rationale: Not discussed in the sources; egalitarian leanings suggest opposition to abolition.

freedom-to-discriminate.rationale: Cultural feminists pursued legal protections for women and opposed discrimination.

elective-rulers.rationale: Women's inclusion in elective politics is central to Addams; inferred.

minority-veto.rationale: Not discussed; veto by one member sits poorly with consensus and fairness; split.

resist-lawless-ruler.rationale: Not discussed; nonviolent resistance is plausible but forceful removal is not.

animal-suffering-matters.rationale: Mary Daly was a vegetarian animal-rights activist who opposed vivisection and fur; she is one figure, and the sources do not show this as a position of the strand as a whole.

animal-use-humane.rationale: Daly opposed vivisection and fur and was a vegetarian, so humane use is not enough for her strand.

noblesse-oblige.rationale: Care ethics stresses responsibility to those in need but not as a privileged class duty; split.

withdraw-from-politics.rationale: Cultural feminists built women's institutions to change society; withdrawal from public affairs contradicts Addams's civic engagement.

mass-culture-pacifies.rationale: Daly's 'foreground' of male-made false images reproduces patriarchy, and cultural feminists criticised pornography and media.

ruling-class-consent.rationale: Daly treats patriarchy as a religion sustained by ritual and culture, not only by force.

native-born-offices.rationale: Not discussed; global sisterhood suggests opposition.

return-lost-territory.rationale: Territorial demands risk war, against Addams's ethic.

antifascism-founding-value.rationale: Opposition to militarist violence suggests sympathy; not discussed.

slavery-not-civil-war-cause.rationale: Not discussed; egalitarian outlook suggests rejection of this view.

preserve-contested-monuments.rationale: Cultural feminists sought to recover women's heritage over male-celebrating monuments; inferred.

male-disadvantage-attention.rationale: Cultural feminism centres women's oppression by patriarchy and Daly said she did not care about men; equal programmes for men are not a priority.

domestic-violence-symmetry.rationale: Cultural feminists see male violence as the product of patriarchy and male aggression, not symmetrical.

institutions-fit-civilization.rationale: Lorde criticised the movement's universalism, but the sources show no position.

military-guardian-role.rationale: Military political role contradicts Addams's rejection of militarism.

paid-care-work.rationale: Care ethics holds care to be valuable and burdening women, supporting recognition of care as work.

filial-duty.rationale: Rich stressed the mother-daughter bond damaged by patriarchy, but filial duty as stated is not discussed.

no-fault-divorce.rationale: Rich saw institutions controlling women, so freeing women to leave marriage fits; not explicit.

individual-pension-accounts.rationale: Care ethics' collective responsibility for dependants suggests public pensions; inferred.

single-official-language.rationale: Daly proposed a women's language and sought to reclaim suppressed ones; inferred.

foreign-land-ownership.rationale: Not discussed; global sisterhood suggests opposition.

consumerism-harmful.rationale: Addams's nourishing of life over acquisition and Daly's critique of the male-made foreground suggest this; inferred.

arm-foreign-insurgents.rationale: Funding violence abroad contradicts the movement's nonviolent ethic.

intervene-in-bloc.rationale: Sending troops into an ally to keep it in a bloc is the military domination Addams rejects as war virtue.

corporate-influence.rationale: Addams-era reform concern with business power; inferred.

pronatalist-incentives.rationale: Rich opposed institutional pressure on motherhood, though mothering was valued; split-leaning negative.

democratic-peace.rationale: Addams favours peaceful civic cooperation; inferred.

non-intervention.rationale: Addams stresses peace but cultural feminists also appealed to global sisterhood; split.

minority-conspiracy.rationale: Conspiracy against a minority is not part of cultural feminism and opposes sisterhood.

abolish-legal-marriage.rationale: Rich criticised motherhood as institution, but cultural feminists did not agree on abolishing legal marriage.

public-access-to-information.rationale: Women's access to hidden knowledge, e.g. Daly's exposure of gynaecology practices, supports openness; inferred.

local-production.rationale: Daly's biophilia and care for nature support local, living economies; inferred.

informal-organisation.rationale: Cultural feminists built small women's groups and collectives rather than parties; Echols records separatist networks.

national-law-over-international.rationale: Addams's international moral consciousness suggests deference to international law; inferred.

religious-nation.rationale: Daly rejects religion-based community identity as patriarchal.

deference-to-leading-power.rationale: Not discussed; hierarchical submission is male-coded; inferred.

regional-revenue-retention.rationale: Care ethics favours sharing resources; inferred.

defeat-communism.rationale: Militant crusade violates the nonviolent ethic.

religion-illusion.rationale: Daly rejected Christianity but turned to Wicca-influenced spirituality, so not a plain atheist stance.

women-equality-needs-economic-change.rationale: Cultural feminists emphasised culture and values over economic transformation, and Daly distrusted equality frameworks; critics complained they depoliticised economics.

socialized-care.rationale: Care ethics values care but cultural feminists valued mothering; split.

cooperative-communities.rationale: Cultural feminists established separate women's communities and cooperatives (Echols), and valued cooperation.

majority-settlement.rationale: Not discussed; coerced settlement conflicts with sisterhood.

holocaust-denial.rationale: Daly compared gynaecological practice to Nazi medical murders; denial is not part of the movement.

criminalize-homosexuality.rationale: Lesbian feminism is central to the movement (Taylor and Rupp).

suppress-opposition.rationale: Suppressing opposition is violence-aligned authority rejected by Addams and adherents.

punish-blasphemy.rationale: Daly rejected religious authority over speech and belief.

colonies-serve-metropole.rationale: Colonial extraction conflicts with sisterhood and the rejection of conquest.

unreligious-rulers-fought.rationale: Violent removal of rulers for religious reasons is opposed by the nonviolence ethic.

participatory-democracy.rationale: Cultural feminists built participatory women's groups; Addams advocates civic participation.

intersecting-oppressions.rationale: Lorde and others criticised cultural feminism for ignoring women of colour, but its core centres patriarchy as a single system; split.

gender-identity-recognition.rationale: Daly argued surgery produces 'feminine persons' but not women, and TERF views trace to cultural feminism (s1).

assisted-dying.rationale: Not discussed; care ethics is ambivalent.

islam-incompatible.rationale: Lorde-style criticism made the movement attend to non-European culture; not discussed, and sisterhood opposes such claims.

divine-source-of-authority.rationale: Daly called a male God implying male supremacy and rejected theological authority.

ban-nda-harassment.rationale: Sexual harassment redress for women fits the movement; inferred.

abolish-armed-forces.rationale: Addams's rejection of war virtues and cultural feminist anti-militarism make abolition a natural extension, though few sources state it.

rich-first.rationale: Care ethics rejects deferred prosperity for the poor; inferred.

stay-neutral-between-blocs.rationale: Addams's peace ideals favour staying out of military blocs; inferred.

property-franchise.rationale: Addams treats the franchise as civic machinery for all, and women's enfranchisement is central.

domination-women-nature.rationale: Daly linked the domination of women and nature as male necrophilia, and Griffin's Woman and Nature is central to the theory (s1).

press-owned-by-wealth.rationale: Not discussed; adherents founded women's presses but the claim is not documented.

racial-franchise.rationale: Addams treats the franchise as universal civic machinery; racial limits conflict with sisterhood.

interfaith-marriage-restriction.rationale: State control of marriage by religion is patriarchal; inferred.

boycott-minority-shops.rationale: Not discussed; conflicts with sisterhood ideal.

reinterpret-religion.rationale: Daly moved beyond Christianity, but reforming feminist theology is part of the broader movement; contested.

open-lgbt-military-service.rationale: Lesbian rights are central but anti-militarism makes military service a mixed question; split.

state-promotes-atheism.rationale: Daly turned to spirituality; state-imposed atheism is not part of the movement.

abolish-police-prisons.rationale: Cultural feminists favoured legal protection against male violence; abolition is not discussed.

charity-over-state-aid.rationale: Care ethics holds public responsibility for dependants; inferred.

existential-risk-priority.rationale: Not discussed; biophilia supports protecting life, but the framing is technocratic.

women-in-religious-leadership.rationale: Daly challenged male-only religious structures and argued a male God implies male supremacy.

shared-marital-authority.rationale: Cultural feminists oppose male authority in the family as part of patriarchy.

foreign-residents-local-vote.rationale: Global sisterhood and inclusion suggest agreement; inferred.

uniformed-youth.rationale: Drilled youth movements are militarist, which Addams rejects.

no-nuclear-weapons-on-territory.rationale: Nuclear weapons exemplify militarism opposed by the movement.

no-foreign-bases.rationale: Peace ideals favour fewer military bases; inferred.

recognise-genocide.rationale: Daly drew the Nazi comparison in her critique of gynaecology; recognition of mass killings fits the movement's values.

income-for-work-not-ownership.rationale: Care ethics values labour including unpaid care; inferred.

never-kill-self-defence.rationale: Nonviolence is valued but self-defence for women was often supported; adherents split.

unbroken-national-continuity.rationale: Women's heritage, not nationhood, is the continuity cultural feminists sought.

sex-socially-constructed.rationale: Cultural feminists treat sex differences as fundamental biology and not constructed, sometimes a source of women's superior value.

no-fixed-category-of-women.rationale: Critics such as Alcoff and Echols describe cultural feminism as affirming a fixed female nature; the answer rests on that characterisation rather than on adherents' own statements.

martyrs-honoured.rationale: Martyr cults tied to war virtues are rejected by Addams; inferred.

politics-spiritual-struggle.rationale: Daly casts patriarchy as a religion and women's liberation as spiritual transformation, with Wiccan influence.

culture-before-state.rationale: Cultural feminism prioritises building women's culture and values over state reform; Echols traces the shift from politics to culture.

god-not-male.rationale: Daly argued that a male God implies male supremacy and called herself post-Christian; the sources show this for Daly, not for cultural feminists generally.

scripture-judged-by-women.rationale: Daly judged religious texts by whether they serve women, though she ultimately abandoned theology as patriarchal.

economy-in-majority-hands.rationale: Not discussed; sisterhood ideal opposes ethnic economic domination.

independent-unions.rationale: Addams-era labour reform favoured worker-run organisation; inferred.

local-essentials-public.rationale: Addams's municipal housekeeping puts local essentials in civic hands.

municipal-property.rationale: Addams favours municipal action on essentials but sources do not endorse municipal ownership of production.

family-wage.rationale: Care ethics and the critique of male-breadwinner structures suggest scepticism; not discussed.

faster-drug-approval.rationale: Daly's critique of male medical practice suggests caution about rushed approvals; inferred.

person-over-state.rationale: Care ethics treats persons as ends in relation to others; inferred.

spiritual-nature.rationale: Daly's Background of connection and Wiccan-influenced spirituality affirm a spiritual dimension.

gm-crops.rationale: Daly's biophilia and distrust of male technological domination suggest scepticism; inferred.

racial-group-interests.rationale: Cultural feminism emphasises women's shared interests; racial group politics conflicts with its sisterhood ideal, though Lorde's critique applied.

defensive-wars-only.rationale: Addams's rejection of conquest and war virtues points to defence only, though adherents often go further to pacifism.

communal-electorates.rationale: Not discussed; separate religious electorates tend to entrench male-led authority.

foreign-partition-plot.rationale: Not discussed; a conspiracy framing not found in the sources.

free-public-college.rationale: Not discussed; inferred from the movement's egalitarian leanings.

women-distinct-values.rationale: Addams and Gilman stressed cooperation, caring and nonviolent conflict resolution as virtues needed from women, and cultural feminism revalues such traits.

pollution-taxes.rationale: Inferred from its reverence for nature and critique of male domination of the earth; the sources do not address taxes versus regulation, so adherents are not placed either way.

future-generations.rationale: Inferred from Daly's biophilia and the movement's nurture-centred ethic of care; the sources do not discuss duties to the unborn directly.

arms-reduction.rationale: Addams's precursor text rejects the war virtues in favour of nurture and peace, and cultural feminism treats militarism as an expression of male aggression.

open-diplomacy.rationale: Inferred from the anti-patriarchal critique of closed elite male power and the stress on cooperation; the sources do not discuss secret treaties.

capital-controls.rationale: The movement's writers do not address capital flows, and nothing in its care-centred principles points clearly either way.

state-arms-monopoly.rationale: Its anti-militarist, anti-violence stance and view of male aggression imply support for disarming private armed groups; inferred.

soldiers-refuse-war.rationale: Addams and later care-ethics writers treat women's peace virtues as a basis for rejecting war, which supports conscientious refusal.

collective-bargaining.rationale: Its cooperative, connection-centred values favour solidarity over individual contracts; inferred.

in-work-tax-credits.rationale: Care ethics treats meeting dependants' needs as a public responsibility, so supplementing low-paid families is a likely inference.

fiscal-rules-binding.rationale: Cooperative, care-centred priorities favour public spending, so binding limits on borrowing are unlikely to be liked; inferred.

restructure-world-economy.rationale: Its anti-patriarchal, cooperative values extend to fairer terms for poorer countries; the movement's writers rarely address it.

smash-state-machine.rationale: It builds parallel women's institutions and rejects patriarchal ones, but rarely discusses seizing or smashing the state; adherents split.

free-economic-experiment.rationale: Building women's businesses and institutions alongside others implies a variety of arrangements, not one blueprint; inferred.

nature-as-capital.rationale: Its reverence for connection to nature suggests that pricing nature as capital would be resisted; inferred.

sacred-nation.rationale: It sees national loyalty and militarism as patriarchal and puts women's community and peace first; inferred.

student-debt-relief.rationale: Care-centred, egalitarian values lean towards relieving debts; the sources do not discuss it.

internal-colonialism.rationale: Not addressed in its core texts.

shared-human-nature.rationale: It holds that women and men differ fundamentally, so a single shared nature is not its framing, though it values dignity; inferred.

public-service-media.rationale: A strong care-based public role and a wish to revalue women's culture suggest support for independent public media; inferred.

religions-one-truth.rationale: Daly treated established religion as an expression of patriarchy and rejected the male God, so a shared truth in all religions is inferred to be doubted; the strand's spiritual feminists are divided.

farm-price-support.rationale: The sources do not discuss farm policy; care for nature points one way and distrust of state programmes another.

keep-nuclear-weapons.rationale: Addams, Ruddick and the movement's nonviolence and anti-militarism imply opposition to nuclear arms; inferred, as the question of unilateral disarmament is not discussed.

workers-own-party.rationale: The strand focused on women's culture and institutions rather than class parties; adherents are split and the sources are silent.

ban-fgm.rationale: The strand's focus on male violence against women and its critique of patriarchy imply support for a legal ban; inferred, as the sources do not discuss it.

women-property-inheritance.rationale: Its critique of patriarchy and attention to women's undervalued status imply equal property and inheritance rights; inferred.

one-language-many-names.rationale: Cultural feminism has no position on language classification.

pollution-tort-liability.rationale: Its reverence for nature and care ethics favour protective regulation of pollution over leaving harm to private suits; inferred.

customary-chiefs-lawmaking.rationale: Cultural feminists hold that patriarchal institutions should be replaced, which makes a formal role for male customary chiefs unlikely to be accepted; inferred.

environment-over-liberty.rationale: Daly's biophilia and the strand's identification with nature imply that nature protection outranks competing freedoms; inferred, and adherents may not word it so.

mandatory-sentences.rationale: The anti-pornography and anti-violence wing favours tough responses to sexual violence while care ethics distrusts punitive approaches, so adherents are split.

immigrants-learn-language.rationale: The sources do not address immigration or language, and adherents are split.

no-compulsory-union.rationale: The movement's sympathies are with collective organising and solidarity among workers, so a ban on compulsory membership is inferred to be disliked; the sources do not discuss unions.

voter-id.rationale: Inferred from the movement's concern with women's access to public life; the sources do not discuss voting rules.

religious-equal-recognition.rationale: Daly attacked patriarchal religion, but the movement also embraced goddess and women's spirituality, so equal legal standing for religious interpretations is a mild inference.

democracy-is-procedure.rationale: The movement locates oppression in patriarchal culture beyond formal institutions, so adherents would not call a system democratic on elections alone, yet it offers no stated view of the definition.

premarital-sex.rationale: Rich and others defended women's sexual self-definition, while the anti-pornography wing criticised commodified sex; acceptance of consensual sex for women is inferred.

internet-shutdowns.rationale: Inferred from its anti-militarist, nonviolent opposition to coercive state power; the sources do not address the internet.

negative-income-tax.rationale: Care-centred principles favour public provision, but cultural feminists wrote little on welfare design and a cash scheme is not clearly opposed or supported.

women-suffrage.rationale: Addams and the movement's precursors treated women's civic participation as essential to bringing nurture and cooperation into public life, which implies equal voting and office-holding rights.

religion-oppresses-women.rationale: Daly described patriarchy as the religion of the planet and rejected the male God, though other cultural feminists embraced women's spirituality, so adherents lean yes but not uniformly.

race-social-construct.rationale: Cultural feminism's essentialism concerned sex, not race, and the sources do not discuss race; agreement with the scholarly view is inferred.

gender-equality-agencies.rationale: The movement built women's institutions and would likely welcome state bodies for women; the sources do not discuss government agencies.

homestead-ownership.rationale: Cultural feminism's nature-connected, cooperative ethos sits uneasily with first-claim private ownership; inferred from that ethos, as the sources do not discuss property.

international-criminal-courts.rationale: Inferred from the anti-militarist, peace-centred values Addams and later cultural feminists stressed; the sources do not discuss tribunals.

scripture-inerrant.rationale: Daly's work rejects patriarchal religion and its scriptural authority as a source of women's oppression.

gendered-self-government.rationale: Inferred from the movement's insistence on women's participation and valued traits in public life; self-government is not addressed directly.

defend-planned-state.rationale: Inferred: hierarchical bureaucratic states and military defence sit poorly with its anti-patriarchal, nonviolent principles; the sources do not address this.

indirect-election.rationale: Inferred from its preference for cooperative, non-hierarchical, participatory forms; the sources do not discuss electoral design.

national-church-status.rationale: Daly's critique treats established patriarchal churches as instruments of women's oppression, so special legal status for one is rejected.

minority-territorial-autonomy.rationale: Inferred from the movement's valuing of distinct cultures and self-determination; not addressed in the sources.

disputed-territory-plebiscite.rationale: Inferred from its participatory and peace-oriented values as a nonviolent way to settle disputes; not addressed in the sources.

keep-colonial-borders.rationale: The movement never addressed borders and no principle clearly points either way.

simple-living.rationale: Inferred from the strand's connection to nature and critique of consumption and domination; sources do not discuss lifestyle directly.

restrict-indigenous-settlement.rationale: Not addressed; its respect for nature and culture and its universalism pull in different directions.

equal-conscription.rationale: Inferred: the strand holds women are more nonviolent and anti-militarist, so it would favour no drafting of anyone; the sources do not state this.

homeland-spiritual-bond.rationale: Inferred from the movement's valuing of connection to nature as a women's trait; national land duty is not discussed.

extrajudicial-killing.rationale: Inferred from its nonviolence and rejection of male aggression; drug policy is not discussed.

protect-kin-minorities.rationale: Inferred from the Addams-style peace and anti-militarist thread, which distrusts nationalist protection claims.

resources-common-ownership.rationale: Inferred from the care-ethics, cooperative outlook, which treats shared goods as shared responsibility.

self-ownership.rationale: Inferred from Daly and Rich's stress on women's control of their own bodies; the sources do not discuss the doctrine.

targeted-social-spending.rationale: Care ethics stresses meeting need through public responsibility, which favours universal provision; inferred.

bypass-parties-groups.rationale: Inferred from the anti-hierarchical, women's-institution-building strategy that prefers organised communities to leader-centred politics.

no-business-privileges.rationale: Inferred from its critique of male-dominated power networks; the sources do not discuss business privilege.

no-denominational-politics.rationale: Inferred from its critique of patriarchal religion, as in Daly; denominational politics is not discussed.

tech-with-ancestral-values.rationale: Daly criticised technology as patriarchal yet revived ancient women's values; the sources do not settle this combination.

wife-divorce-without-consent.rationale: Inferred from the movement's opposition to patriarchal control of women's lives; divorce law is not discussed.

distribution-by-process.rationale: Inferred from care ethics' concern with outcomes for the dependent and disadvantaged.

financial-transactions-tax.rationale: Inferred from its anti-exploitation and anti-militarist stance; the sources do not discuss financial taxes.

racism-not-main-obstacle.rationale: Inferred from its view that patriarchy is the root oppression; race is not discussed in the sources.

unjust-law-not-binding.rationale: Daly's moral critique of patriarchal institutions implies unjust rules lack authority; inferred.

multipolar-world.rationale: Addams's peace writing favours international cooperation over bloc rivalry; the question is not addressed.

labour-theory-of-value.rationale: Inferred from care ethics' point that women's care labour is undervalued; the theory is not named.

patriotism-serves-workers.rationale: Addams and the anti-militarist thread distrust nationalism; inferred.

material-over-identity.rationale: The movement stresses culture and identity over economic politics, as critics note, so it opposes putting material interests first.

market-under-party-rule.rationale: Inferred from its anti-authoritarian, anti-patriarchal stance; the sources do not discuss this model.

missingStatements.text: Women tend to bring distinct values, such as care, cooperation and nonviolence, to public life, and these should be given more weight.
missingStatements.rationale: Addams and Gilman stressed cooperation, caring and nonviolent conflict resolution as virtues needed from women, and cultural feminism revalues such traits.

missingStatements.text: Women should have spaces and institutions of their own, closed to men.
missingStatements.rationale: Cultural feminists built women's businesses and cultures, and Daly excluded men from some advanced classes to protect discussion.
missingStatements.declined: Narrow question about women-only institutions within feminism; few other ideologies take a side, so it would add an unanswerable burden to every audit.

notes: Positions on gender essentialism, pornography, nature and peace are well documented; economics and constitutional questions are mostly inferences. Strands: Daly's separatist post-Christian line differs from Gilligan-Ruddick care ethics, which denies women are inherently different (Gilligan found women as likely to use justice reasoning, via SEP).
